property_summary: Only the owner can successfully call withdrawAll (non-owners cannot withdrawAll).
Only the contract owner can successfully call withdrawAll (calls by non-owners revert).
Calls to withdrawAll revert when msg.sender is not the contract owner.
On the original contract, withdrawAll should revert for non-owners (this contract is not the deployer).
On the original contract, calling withdrawAll from this test's caller (which is not the contract owner) should revert.

Rule: Only the deployer (owner) can withdraw contract funds, so calling withdrawAll() after sendMoney(...) leaves the contract balance equal to zero when the caller is the owner; the mutant inverts onlyOwner so a non-owner can withdraw, breaking this property for some caller/address and value.

For any address attacker and any nonzero amount funded to C via sendMoney(attacker, amount) that the owner initiated, the reference contract ensures only the deployer (owner) can withdraw those funds (so address(c).balance == 0 after owner calls withdrawAll), whereas the mutant inverts onlyOwner allowing a non-owner attacker to withdraw and thus can make address(c).balance == 0 when the attacker attempts withdrawal — the property: after owner attempts withdrawAll the contract balance becomes zero (reference always), but the mutant lets a non-owner withdraw first so this rule can be violated for some inputs.

For all caller addresses and amounts that the deployer (owner) sends through sendMoney to an external contract which reverts on receive, the reference contract C guarantees the owner can still withdraw the contract balance (withdrawAll succeeds and empties the contract), whereas the mutant that inverts onlyOwner allows a non-owner to withdraw (or causes owner withdrawals to be disallowed), so the property (owner can withdraw leaving address(c).balance == 0) is violated for some inputs when the modifier is inverted.

For every caller address and amount (admissible inputs) if the contract has nonzero balance, the deployer (owner) can always call withdrawAll to empty the contract balance; the mutant inverting onlyOwner prevents the owner from withdrawing (or allows non-owners instead) and so this property is violated for some inputs.

For all addresses attacker and all nonzero amounts value that are sent into C via its fallback (by sending Ether to the contract), the deployer (owner) can always call withdrawAll and empty the contract (address(c).balance == 0); the mutant inverting onlyOwner prevents the owner from withdrawing, so for some inputs the balance remains nonzero.

For any caller who is the owner and any contract balance > 0, calling withdrawAll() causes the contract's balance to become zero (full withdrawal); the mutant that calls withdraw(0) can leave a positive balance and thus violates this.

For any owner caller and any positive contract balance funded via fallback, calling withdrawAll() makes the contract balance zero (reference): the mutant withdrawing 0 can leave a nonzero contract balance, violating this property.

For any owner caller and any positive contract balance, calling withdrawAll() reduces the contract balance to zero (reference does this by withdrawing address(this).balance; the mutant withdraws 0 and can leave a nonzero balance).

For any owner caller and any positive contract balance funded by sending ether to the contract, calling withdrawAll() results in the contract balance becoming zero (reference); the mutant that calls withdraw(0) can leave a non-zero contract balance, so the property is violated for some inputs.

For any owner caller and any contract balance funded by a prior payable call, invoking withdrawAll() causes the contract balance to become zero (reference withdraws full balance); the mutant that calls withdraw(0) can leave a non-zero balance and thus violates this property for some inputs.

For any caller who is owner and any contract balance, calling withdrawAll transfers the entire contract balance out (leaving address(c).balance == 0); the mutant that withdraws only half violates this for some balances.

For any initial contract balance and owner invoking withdrawAll, the reference empties the contract (address(c).balance == 0) while the mutant that withdraws only half can leave a non-zero balance for some initial balances.

For any nonzero contract balance and when the owner calls withdrawAll, the reference contract empties the contract (address(c).balance becomes 0) — the mutant that withdraws only half can leave a nonzero balance for some initial balances, so there exists an input (initial balance) where address(c).balance != 0 after withdrawAll.

For any nonzero initial contract balance funded by the owner and any owner calling withdrawAll, the reference contract transfers the entire balance out so address(c).balance == 0 after the call; the mutant that withdraws only half can leave a nonzero balance for some initial balances, violating this.

For any nonzero initial contract balance funded by ANY address and when the owner calls withdrawAll, the reference contract reduces address(c).balance by exactly that initial balance (empties the contract), while the mutant that withdraws only half will leave address(c).balance equal to half the initial balance for some initial balances — therefore the general rule: after owner calls withdrawAll the contract balance becomes zero; the mutant violates this for some initial balances.

Invariant: only the contract owner can successfully invoke withdrawAll() (so calling withdrawAll() does not change the contract balance unless msg.sender == owner); the mutant removes the onlyOwner guard so a non-owner can drain the contract and violate this rule.

For any caller and any funded contract balance, only the deployer (owner) can make the contract's balance drop to zero by calling withdrawAll; the mutant (which removes onlyOwner) allows some non-owner caller to drain the contract, violating this rule for some fuzzed caller and value.

For every caller and every nonzero deposited amount, only the owner (deployer) can cause the contract's balance to decrease when calling withdrawAll; the mutant removing onlyOwner allows some non-owner caller to make the contract balance decrease, violating that rule for some fuzzed caller and deposit amount.

For every caller and any initial contract balance, calling withdrawAll only changes the contract balance if the caller is the owner; the mutant (which removes the onlyOwner check) allows some non-owner caller to change (drain) the contract balance, violating this rule for some fuzzed caller and amount.

For every caller and any deposited amount, only the contract owner can successfully withdraw all funds via withdrawAll(); the mutant removing the onlyOwner guard allows some non-owner caller (an adversarial attacker) to call withdrawAll and make the contract's balance drop (or drain) for some fuzzed caller/amount.

For any caller who is the owner and any non-negative ETH balance in the contract, calling withdrawAll always reduces the contract balance to zero (reference holds for all inputs); the mutant that makes withdrawAll a no-op can leave a non-zero balance, violating this rule for some inputs.

For any owner caller and any initial contract balance > 0, calling withdrawAll as the owner makes the contract balance zero; the mutant that makes withdrawAll a no-op can leave a positive balance, violating this rule.

For any caller that is the contract owner and any initial contract balance (>=0) provided via a payable deposit to the contract, calling withdrawAll reduces the contract balance to zero; the mutant that makes withdrawAll a no-op can leave a non-zero balance and thus violate this.

For any owner caller and any positive contract balance funded by sending Ether to the contract, calling withdrawAll as the owner transfers all contract Ether out so that address(c).balance becomes 0; the mutant that makes withdrawAll a no-op can leave a positive balance, violating this property.

For any owner caller and any positive initial contract balance funded by sending Ether via a low-level call through an adversarial callee that accepts funds, calling withdrawAll will make the contract balance zero (reference transfers out all Ether to owner; the mutant no-op can leave balance > 0).
After the owner withdraws all funds via withdrawAll(), the contract balance becomes zero (all Ether is removed).
Withdraw called by the owner never reverts (i.e., withdraw always succeeds when called by the contract owner).
When the owner calls withdraw(0) it should not revert (i.e., owner calls to withdraw must succeed).
When the owner calls withdraw(0) it should not revert (i.e., owner calls to withdraw must succeed).
The test asserts that when the owner calls withdraw(0) on C, the call does not revert (i.e., !reverted).

For any callee that reverts when sent Ether, the reference contract's withdraw path (which uses transfer) ensures prior failed external send in sendMoney does not prevent owner from later withdrawing contract balance, while the mutant (which uses call + require) can cause the contract to become unable to withdraw funds after such a revert; the property asserts that after calling sendMoney to a reverting helper, withdrawAll still succeeds (owner gets funds) — which holds for reference but is broken by the mutant for some inputs.

If the contract's owner calls sendMoney to an external callee that reverts when receiving Ether, the reference implementation still allows the owner to successfully withdraw the contract's balance afterwards, whereas the mutant that uses call+require in withdraw can become unable to withdraw after such an interaction.

For any attacker contract that reverts on receiving Ether and any nonzero amount sent into C, the reference implementation always allows the owner to withdraw the contract balance afterwards (withdrawAll succeeds), whereas the mutant using call+require in withdraw can be made to block withdrawAll after the failing external interaction.

For any nonzero amount sent into C and after calling sendMoney to a callee that reverts on receiving Ether, the reference contract still allows the owner to withdraw the contract's full balance via withdrawAll, but the mutant (which uses call+require in withdraw) can be made to fail withdrawing after such an interaction.

For any nonzero amount deposited into C and after calling sendMoney(...) to an external callee that REVERTs on receive, the reference contract still allows the owner to withdraw the contract's full balance via withdrawAll (owner receives the funds), whereas the mutant (which uses call+require in withdraw) can cause withdrawAll to fail; thus the property: after sending to a reverting callee, withdrawAll still succeeds (owner can collect the contract balance).
Only the contract owner can withdraw funds from C, so after sending funds into C, a non-owner cannot decrease C's balance via withdraw.
